blocks.note: `nb` (64), the bound the engine's alias sweep walks within
`fc`, one channel of a packed colour widened to the 0..255 the escape wants (`(c >> shift & 15) * 17`) — the sibling the grammar names after it

the colour the escapes carry: `Ff`, which answers the sentinel unchanged and otherwise un-packs the three channels back to their own shifts, and `pc`, which packs two of them into one word — a pair is the foreground and the background

the SGR the surface measures its work in: `_s` the code table (38/48 set, 39/49 reset, 2 truecolor), `Hf` the parameter list for one side, `gc` the pair of sequences for a colour, `hc` the sequence a fresh paint starts from, and `Sc` (1024) the slot capacity

the surface state and the matcher: `lb`, which builds the slots/held/table/probe/aliases row (including the `Uint8Array(Sc * gn.width)` cell table and its one-cell probe), `cb` the slots a paint has not touched, oldest first, `ub` (16384) the alias bound, and `db`, which scores every slot against the probe by squared channel distance — counting `Lr.defaultMismatch` where a default flag differs — and answers the closest
`gb` (1024) and `hb` (131072), the two numbers the engine spends and bounds its work with: the cost of reusing a slot, and the cap on what one paint may evaluate

the engine and the rows it writes: `gNs`, whose `beginPaint` admits the frame's keys (a free slot or the stalest one, each admitted through the token row), rewrites the table, and whose `sgrOf` answers a key's escape — reusing what the last paint placed, then a slot matched by `db`, and answering the held escape when neither applies — with `size()` and `standing()` beside it; `_b`, which turns a frame into the distinct colour runs a row is made of; and `Lss`, which walks the frame row by row, emitting an escape only when the colour changes and a character for every cell

the terminal grammar the CSI helper is written against: `xse` the C0 code points, `PH` the escape, `nG` the bell, `Y9e` the parameter separator, `fRr` the charset reset, and `CZ` the introducer bytes (CSI 91, OSC 93, DCS 80, APC 95, PM 94, SOS 88, ST 92)
`A`, the CSI introducer built from the grammar (esc plus the CSI byte), and `S`, the parameter/intermediate/final byte ranges

`fl`, the CSI helper the SGR builder writes every sequence with: no argument answers the bare introducer, one argument appends it, and more join all but the last with the separator and append the last
